questions.title: Kitchen and Restaurant Operations; Hygiene, Safety and Security

subQuestions.questionText: Scenario: Sam, a skilled chef, is often sick which affects his work negatively. He has been diagnosed with HIV and because he fears the stigma, he decides to keep his status a secret. His occasional absence from work causes a strain on his colleagues. Discuss how Sam's absence from work affects staff productivity and the business operations of the hotel.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 3) (3 marks)
• There will be workflow disruption due to shortage of 1 staff member / takes longer to do the task / shortage of skills / business operations negatively impacted as it may result in a limited menu
• It will reduce productivity / reduce service delivery / slow service
• Staff morale will be low
• Employees can experience fatigue because of the extra workload / staff will be strained / overloaded
• There will be temporary / vacant posts available and the employer will have to hire new / temporary employees
• The employer will have to retrain the employees which will lead to time loss
• The business will lose income / profit
• Increase the cost due to rehiring and retraining

subQuestions.questionText: Justify why Sam should not be restricted from work based on his HIV status.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
Sam cannot be restricted from work because:
• a food-service worker infected with HIV needn't be restricted from work unless they have other infections (such as diarrhoea, hepatitis or TB)
• the transmission of HIV/Aids in food and beverages is not a risk
• HIV/Aids cannot be transmitted by sharing utensils such as knives and forks / using the same bathroom facilities / cannot be transferred by touching or being close to each other
• as long as Sam follows all standard hygiene practices, he is not a threat to others
• it is against the law to discriminate against a person who is HIV positive
• there should be no infringement of human rights against privacy

subQuestions.questionText: Scenario: Mr Smith and his family made a booking at the Earthland Hotel using the online reservation system. Explain the benefits of using the online reservation system for the Smith family.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 4) (4 marks)
The online reservation system will allow:
• guest to book rooms on a computer by making use of online security
• the online security to protect the privacy and financial information of the guests
• hotels / rooms to be compared on prices and facilities
• special deals and information on prices to be easily accessible / it may be cheaper to book ahead of time
• last minute bookings to be made easily / convenient / at any time of the day or night
• guest to have access to an electronic hotel system which saves money and time / fast / quick
• universal access / online access from the comfort of home
• the room to be secured ahead of time / instant confirmation
• administration upon arrival to be limited
• reviews from previous guests' experiences to be accessed
• fewer mistakes as customers' data is captured automatically
• personal information to be stored for future reference
• proof of communication for the guest and the establishment / going paperless

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how computers facilitate the process of checking in upon arrival.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 3) (3 marks)
• The name will be entered on the computer and a registration card will be printed

• Guest can check in while in the hotel lounge / at home to prevent long queues
• At the same time during check-in, the guest's account is created / confirms the amount already paid

He was rude and not willing to assist. Criticise Jacob's professional work ethics.

Jacob was unprofessional and displayed the following:

subQuestions.questionText: Case study: Hospitality Studies learners from Berlin High School must plan and host a corporate cocktail function for guests in the school restaurant, from 18:00 to 20:00. Menu: Smoked Salmon Canapés, Mini Beef Sandwiches, Bacon-stuffed Mushrooms, Mini Fruit Skewers, Chocolate Truffles. Determine when the cocktail snacks should be ready for service.
subQuestions.memoText: • 30 minutes before the function starts / 17:30 / 18:00 / 6 pm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify why the snacks in the menu are suitable to serve at a cocktail function.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 3) (3 marks)
• The snacks are small bite-sized / finger foods / mini snacks
• The snacks include a variety of flavours / ingredients / savoury (bacon-stuffed mushrooms, smoked salmon canapés, beef sandwiches) and sweet (mini fruit skewers, chocolate truffles)
• Guests can pick up snacks with their hands / no utensils needed / not messy / no bones to be discarded
• Hot and cold snacks are included / variety of temperatures
• There is a variety of shapes
• There is a variety of colours
• There is a variety of textures – soft (bacon-stuffed mushrooms, chocolate truffles) and crunchy/crispy (mini fruit skewers, smoked salmon canapés)
• The snacks can be served attractively and creatively
• The menu caters for different customers / religions / cultures

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the choice of EACH of the cocktail snacks for a Hindu guest.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 5) (5 marks)
Not suitable:
• Mini Beef Sandwiches – the Hindu guest will not consume beef / the cow is believed to be sacred
• Bacon-stuffed Mushrooms – Hindu guest will not consume pork products
• Smoked Salmon Canapés – Orthodox Hindu guests do not consume fish / they are mostly vegan
• Chocolate Truffles – contain egg yolk / alcohol which is not suitable for Orthodox Hindu guests
Suitable:
• Mini Fruit Skewers – Hindu guests can consume fruits even if they follow a strict vegetarian diet
• Chocolate Truffles – Hindu guests do consume milk products / there is no alcohol or egg in the truffles
• Smoked Salmon Canapés – Hindu guests do eat fish

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the learners should set up the restaurant for the cocktail function.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 4) (4 marks)
• Set up the tables and chairs scattered around the venue / chairs randomly arranged / against the wall / in clusters
• Allow space for guests to move around
• Provide a couple of round high tables at which guests can gather
• Place a central table for the display of food / set up buffet tables for snacks if self-service will be used
• The buffet table should have a centre piece / focus point / flower arrangement / hors d'oeuvres placed on different levels for attractive appearance
• Use candles / fairy lights to create an ambience / set the tone / atmosphere
• Use decorations / linen to match the theme
• Place tablecloths on the tables / tablecloths must hang to the floor / equally on all sides
• Set up the necessary audio-visual equipment for speeches / sound system for music
• Place cutlery holders on the buffet tables / scattered around / no utensils on the table
• Place the cold snacks on the table before guests arrive
• Place a separate table for the beverages / mocktails
• Have small collection tables for dirty dishes / glasses
• Maintain a comfortable room temperature

subQuestions.questionText: Cost of dishes: Smoked Salmon Canapés R500,00; Mini Beef Sandwiches R640,00; Bacon-stuffed Mushrooms R500,00; Mini Fruit Skewers R360,00; Chocolate Truffles R450,00. Overheads: R150,00. Labour: R100,00 per hour for two cleaners. Calculate the food cost of the cocktail function. Show ALL calculations.
Calculate the selling price of the cocktail function using a food cost percentage of 40%. Show ALL formulas and calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Selling price = food cost ÷ food cost %
= R2 450 ÷ 40% (0,40)
= R6 125 (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the net profit. Show ALL formulas and calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Net profit = Selling price − Total cost (FC + LC + OC)
= R6 125 − [R2 450 + R150 + R400 (R100 × 2 hours × 2 cleaners)]
= R6 125 − R3 000
= R3 125
OR
= R6 125 − [R2 450 + R150 + R200 (R100 × 2 hours for 2 cleaners)]
= R6 125 − R2 800
= R3 325 (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Scenario: Thandeka bought one-litre sachets of fresh milk at a supermarket. Describe the preservation method used for the milk in the sachets.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
Pasteurisation:
• the milk is heated to 72/71 °C for 15 seconds, then cooled to 4 °C, destroying some microorganisms
• is a preservation method that inactivates enzymes / makes enzymes inactive

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO other methods that could be used to preserve milk for a month or longer. Distinguish between the two methods. Tabulate your answer (Preservation method A and B, with a distinguishing point for each).
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2 preservation methods + differences each) (6 marks: 1 + 1 for methods, 2 + 2 for distinguishing)
Sterilising / boiling:
• boiling the milk above 100 °C / higher than boiling point / no moisture is removed
• boiling will eliminate / kill microorganisms / no growth of bacteria
• hermetic sealing prevents microorganisms from entering
Freezing:
• milk is frozen and temperatures lowered to below 0 °C / no higher than −18 °C / no moisture removed
• microorganisms are not killed / eliminated; growth of bacteria is reduced / retarded / inactivated
Drying / dehydrating:
• heat is used to remove moisture
• microorganisms will not grow because of the lack of moisture
UHT / Ultra High Temperature Treatment / Ultra Heat Treated:
• milk is exposed to special heat treatment and packaging process
• milk is exposed to a high temperature of 140 °C for 2–4 seconds and immediately cooled to room temperature
• pure milk, no preservatives added; micro-organisms are destroyed
Canning:
• the milk is heated to a high temperature to reduce moisture
• for condensed milk, sugar is added as a preservative
• for evaporated milk, full-cream milk is pasteurised first, then concentrated by evaporating a fairly large volume of water under vacuum
• milk is hermetically sealed in a tin / can

subQuestions.questionText: Extract: Many countries have seen an increase in people following a vegan diet. However, the main health concern for vegans is how to include sufficient nutrients in their diet. The solution is to include a variety of plant-based products such as grains, nuts, seeds and dried pulses. Suggest TWO pulses that can be included in a vegan diet.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2 relevant pulses) (2 marks)
• Dried beans: Red kidney / Butter / Lima / Broad / Fava / Soybeans / Cannellini / White / Sugar / Black / Mung / Moong / Ditlhodi / Haricot / Pinto
• Lentils / Dhal / Masoor / yellow / red / orange / black / brown lentils
• Chickpeas / Wholegram
• Split peas / yellow split peas / green split peas
• Black-eye peas / -beans / Cowpea

subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why veganism is gaining popularity in many countries.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 4) (4 marks)
• As a result of moral grounds / ethics – object to the killing of animals / opposed to eating animals
• For health reasons – because of high levels of cholesterol and hormones in meat / exclusion of meat prevents heart disease, obesity and diabetes
• For religious / cultural beliefs that may prohibit the eating of meat
• To be environmentally friendly / the meat industry is said to have a negative impact on the environment / for the sustainability of the planet / to lessen the carbon footprint
• Some people do not like the taste of meat
• Meat is more expensive than plant products
• Increased awareness in the media to promote veganism
• Increased variety and availability of vegan food

subQuestions.questionText: Justify why adding nuts and seeds in the vegan diet is nutritionally beneficial.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 4) (4 marks)
Nuts and seeds are a good source of:
• Protein
• Vitamin B
• High in fat but low in cholesterol / healthy fat / unsaturated fat
• Minerals (magnesium, phosphorous, potassium, manganese)
• Fibre / complex carbohydrates
• Vitamin E, which is a good antioxidant
• Omega 6
• Low GI / slowly digestible / slow release of energy

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend storage guidelines for the trifle if it is not served on the day it has been prepared.

• Cover to prevent cross contamination / airtight container

subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the crème pâtissière must be allowed to boil during cooking.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
• To fully gelatinise the starch
• To thicken enough to hold its shape / to reach the correct consistency
• To avoid a starchy taste due to uncooked starch

subQuestions.questionText: Argue whether milk chocolate is a good choice for making chocolate decorations for the trifle.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1 mark for suitable/not suitable + 2 motivations) (3 marks)
Not a good choice / not suitable:
• because it contains milk solids and sugar
• milk solids are intolerant to heat, making the chocolate unsuitable for cooking and baking
• the chocolate may seize / harden and become granular and cause a fatty result / fat separates
• only suitable as an eating chocolate / commercial chocolate
OR
Good choice / Suitable:
• it is cheap
• only suitable if not melted / heated / it can be grated / shaved / finely chopped
• Couverture / compound milk chocolate can be used, however it needs to be tempered / baking milk chocolate can be used as it contains a high vegetable fat content
• it will add colour and flavour / enhance the appearance of the dessert

subQuestions.questionText: FRENCH CRULLERS recipe (Yield 15). Method: 1. Add butter and sugar to hot water and heat until butter has melted. 2. As soon as the water starts boiling, add the flour and salt at once. 3. Stir until the mixture forms a paste and leaves the sides of the saucepan. 4. Allow mixture to cool, add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition. 5. Pipe circles onto greaseproof paper. 6. Slide crullers into heated oil. 7. Fry until golden brown and drain. Predict the outcome of the French crullers if the water boils for 5 minutes during Step 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
If the water boils for five minutes:
• too much water will evaporate / the ratio will be altered / resulting in too little steam development
• final product will be reduced in volume
• the quantity of the product will be less
• the end product will be hard / tough

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why extra flour should NOT be added to the paste in Step 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
• Ungelatinised starch will cause the French crullers to collapse
• No cavity will form / decrease in volume
• The pastry will be too thick / heavy / not have the correct consistency
• It will change the ratio of the pastry
• The end product will be tough / starchy

subQuestions.questionText: Comment on the benefits of following the actions in Step 4.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 2) (2 marks)
• The paste must be cooled completely to prevent over-coagulation
• Adding beaten egg bit by bit / one by one will ensure the paste reaches the correct consistency / it will be thick, smooth, shiny and flow slowly from a spoon
• Ensures the paste will be smooth, pliable to pipe and not be runny
• Beating after each addition of egg ensures emulsification of the mixture

subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the raw French cruller circles should NOT be placed in cold oil during frying.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 1) (1 mark)
• It will absorb oil / will be too oily
• It will not rise properly / it will not form a cavity / small volume
• It will sink to the bottom

subQuestions.questionText: Pictures: T-BONE STEAK (AAA roller mark) and KUDU FILLET (no roller mark). Name the meat cut from which the T-bone steak is obtained.
subQuestions.memoText: Loin (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between a T-bone steak and a Porterhouse steak.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 1 point per steak) (2 marks)
T-bone steak:
• Cut from the loin
• Has a small piece of fillet on one side and a large eye muscle on the other side
Porterhouse steak:
• Cut from the loin next to the rump
• Larger than the T-bone and has a bigger piece of fillet / it is 50 mm thick

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend the most suitable cooking method for the T-bone steak. Motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 1 method + motivation) (2 marks)
Method: Grilling / braai / frying / roasting / oven roasting / dry heat cooking methods are most suitable.
Motivation:
• T-bone is from the hindquarter
• It is a tender meat cut / AAA young animal
• T-bone has less connective tissue and more muscle fibre, making dry heat methods suitable
• Muscle fibre must just coagulate – the internal temperature is low

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the characteristics of the kudu fillet with those of the T-bone steak under the following headings: Marbling, Fat, Bone. Tabulate your answer.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the procedure the waiter should follow when crumbing down during a formal four-course meal.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Any 4) (4 marks)
The waiter must:
• Perform the procedure after the main course and before serving the dessert
• Remove any other unnecessary items
• Hold a plate on the flat of the left hand
• Fold a service cloth and hold it in the right hand or between a spoon and a fork / use a crumbing down brush
• Start on the right-hand side / left side of the host
• Stand between two guests
• Brush down half way from both guests onto the plate using the folded service cloth
• Pull the handle of the dessert cutlery, facing you, from both guests downwards / vertical
• Continue anticlockwise, crumbing down and pulling down cutlery by the stem
• Finish with the host

• Take charge of the situation
• Be polite and friendly without being familiar
• Be attentive but do not respond to the flirting
• Serve the meal as quickly as possible
• If the situation gets out of hand, call the maître d' or restaurant manager
• Request another waiter of a different gender to take over the table
• If the guest continues and the situation gets out of hand, ask security to escort the guest out
